title: Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture
summary: define the docs_subscope default, registered collection customisations, toolbar ownership, public isolation, and lifecycle integration
content_html:
Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture

Architecture Outcome

Every configured one-level sub-scope uses the same docs_subscope engine and one useful default. A sub-scope may select a registered customisation module when its own content or workflow needs more than that default.

configured collection
  -> docs_subscope engine
  -> default presentation and Manage actions
  -> optional registered collection customisation

The customisation is an explicit property of the collection, not an inferred variant of viewer_report, a filename convention, or a condition on a known scope or sub-scope ID.

Collection And Host Identity

The collection remains {scope, sub_scope}. Child documents remain exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} targets.

The indexed host is an ordinary parent-scope document containing:

viewer_report: docs_subscope
viewer_report_access: local
viewer_report_subscope: <sub-scope-id>

The host selects the engine and collection only. The configured sub-scope record selects a known customisation identity; absence means the default. Config must never contain an arbitrary JavaScript module path.

Definition Of The Default

The default is the complete minimum useful report for an ordinary flat document collection. It is not Analysis/Tags with optional labels removed.

Shared public-safe behaviour:

  • collection validation and ordered membership;
  • list, detail, empty, unavailable, and error states;
  • title search over the loaded collection;
  • validated by-ID loading and subdoc navigation; and
  • clean absence of management controls.

Default Manage behaviour adds:

  • status and non-viewable presentation from the compact Manage row;
  • title-ascending initial order and a two-state sort control switching between title ascending and last_updated descending;
  • exact-collection New document, including for an empty collection;
  • collection-local checkbox selection, Select all, Clear, and Done;
  • the Actions menu and checked-ID Prepare Package;
  • validated-detail Delete and Copy Link;
  • mounted collection/detail publication for the app-level Import owner; and
  • capability-aware omitted or disabled states without target fallback.

The recency order places missing or unusable last_updated values after dated records, then uses title ascending and doc_id as deterministic tie-breakers. Changing sort does not change checked IDs. Select all and Shift-range consume the current visible sorted projection.

Copy Link follows the existing main-index convention: it copies a Markdown link whose label is the document title and whose destination is the exact viewer URL for the validated sub-scope document, including its report host and subdoc identity. It does not copy a source, payload, or management-service URL.

Filters beyond title search, additional columns, additional row fields, and additional actions are customisations. A customisation may add to the default; it does not silently remove or replace default behaviour.

The public manifest remains:

{
  "docs": [
    {"doc_id": "d-*", "title": "Title"}
  ]
}

The standard Manage row is:

{
  "doc_id": "d-*",
  "title": "Title",
  "ui_status": "",
  "viewable": true,
  "last_updated": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
}

last_updated is standard because the default visibly consumes it for recency sorting. The Manage manifest remains a data projection, not an action registry.

Isolated Candidate And Cutover

SSR-1 develops the default through an explicitly temporary local-only report identity, provisionally docs_subscope_candidate.

The candidate copies the current shared report module so work on its structure cannot regress the canonical docs_subscope used by Analysis/Tags. Copying the report module alone is insufficient: the Manage host currently gives every docs_subscope the same contribution containing New, selection, Prepare Package, Delete, row state, and Import-context publication. The candidate must therefore receive its own default Manage composition as well.

The isolation boundary is narrow:

  • copy the shared report module that is being reworked;
  • add a local-only loader and explicit temporary Manage dispatch;
  • create a new default Manage contribution rather than changing the existing Tags-shaped contribution in place;
  • reuse generic filter, URL, target, action, selection, and lifecycle helpers where their contracts already fit; and
  • reuse the one sub-scope builder and its public/Manage manifest generation.

The candidate is not added to the public report loader. Its Studio host uses the temporary report ID only while SSR-1 is active; final host front matter uses canonical viewer_report: docs_subscope.

Because the builder is shared, SSR-1.1 may add the harmless standard last_updated field and dormant registered-projector support, but it preserves the existing root groups and row group output for the still-live Tags path. It does not reinterpret document_groups as the new settings object. SSR-1.2 switches Tags config, builder projection, and browser composition together, then removes the old direct group projection in that same cutover.

Cutover occurs only after the studio/default empty/list/detail/action surface is accepted and Analysis/Tags passes parity through its registered customisation. In the same delivery:

  1. canonical docs_subscope resolves the accepted implementation;
  2. the Studio fixture host switches to canonical docs_subscope;
  3. Analysis/Tags switches to canonical default plus its customisation; and
  4. the candidate report registry row, loader entry, temporary Manage dispatch, and superseded module/contribution wiring are removed.

There is no permanent alias and no runtime condition on sub_scope: default.

Persistence And Propagation

The default is persisted as one canonical implementation, not as a copied report attached to each sub-scope. studio/default remains a permanent local reference instance, but it is not the source of the implementation.

concern canonical authority
Shared list/detail behaviour Canonical docs_subscope runtime module
Default Manage controls and lifecycle publication Canonical default Manage contribution
Default public and Manage manifest fields Shared sub-scope builder
One collection instance Sub-scope config, report-host document, and child source documents
Additional collection behaviour Registered customisation selected by that sub-scope
Default review and regression surface Permanent studio/default reference instance

An ordinary live instance persists only its collection and host identity:

report host: viewer_report = docs_subscope
report host: viewer_report_subscope = projects
sub-scope config: no customisation identity

It does not receive a JavaScript copy or version of the default. Each mount loads the current canonical docs_subscope implementation. Absence of a customisation identity selects the default path, so an uncustomised dotlineform/projects and any later lifecycle-created collection receive the same implementation automatically.

Generated manifest.json and manage-manifest.json files persist one collection's current data projection. They are not templates, code, or the definition of the default and must not be hand-maintained as such.

Changes propagate through their owning layer:

  • a shared list/detail or presentation change updates the canonical report module and reaches every mounted instance when current assets are loaded;
  • a default management change updates the canonical default Manage contribution and reaches every manageable instance;
  • a default manifest-field change updates the shared builder and requires the affected configured sub-scopes to be rebuilt so their generated projections match the runtime contract;
  • a customisation change updates its registered builder/browser parts and affects only collections selecting that identity; and
  • a configuration-shape change also regenerates browser configuration before affected reports are reviewed.

Runtime and builder changes to one manifest contract ship as one coordinated change. The runtime may define contained missing-value behaviour, such as undated rows sorting last, but stale manifests are not a second supported implementation.

Default changes are first exercised on studio/default, then checked against Analysis/Tags as a customised consumer. Changes that alter the public-safe path also receive public-route evidence. After cutover the Studio host uses canonical docs_subscope permanently; only the development candidate and its temporary registry/dispatch are removed.

Customisation Resolution

A sub-scope selects a customisation with one strict object:

{
  "report_customisation": {
    "id": "analysis_tags",
    "settings": {
      "groups": ["subject", "domain", "form", "theme"]
    }
  }
}

Absence of report_customisation means the default. The object accepts only id and settings; id matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, and settings is an object validated by that identity's registry entry. It may be empty only when that entry permits it. Analysis/Tags requires one ordered, non-empty, duplicate-free groups list. Its existing top-level document_groups field is removed during SSR-1.2 rather than retained as an alias. Metadata validation, mutation, package validation, builder projection, and browser controls all consume the same normalized customisation settings.

A controlled registry maps each known customisation identity to its allowed parts:

sub-scope config identity and validated settings
  -> builder projector for each permitted access
  -> browser-config descriptor for each permitted access
  -> public browser factory, when registered
  -> Manage browser factory, when registered

The Python registry owns settings validation and data projection. Separate static JavaScript registries own public and Manage factories. A focused agreement check requires the IDs and declared access surfaces to match; config never contains a module path, export name, field list, or handler. The first registered identity is analysis_tags.

The generated Manage browser config carries the normalized descriptor needed to resolve analysis_tags. Because that customisation has no public contribution, its public browser config omits the descriptor and the public report follows the default path. A later public contribution must be declared public in the Python registry and the public JavaScript registry; only its public-safe descriptor is projected.

For Analysis/Tags the generated Manage record contains only:

{
  "report_customisation": {"id": "analysis_tags"}
}

The browser-config controller normalizes that to reportCustomisation: {id}. Raw source settings are not copied into browser config; browser-required data comes from the access-specific manifest projector.

Unknown identities or malformed settings fail scope-config loading. A missing builder projector or registry disagreement fails generation or its focused contract check. If generated browser config names an unavailable module, or a module import/factory fails, the report renders a contained error and does not silently fall back to the default. Absence is the only default selector.

Current Implementation Trace

Current owner Current responsibility SSR-1 disposition
docs_scope_config.py Normalizes sub-scope titles, capabilities, statuses, and top-level document_groups Add strict report_customisation; move group settings into analysis_tags
docs_builder/sub_scope.py Builds both manifests and currently projects root groups and row group directly Retain default fields; delegate only the custom namespace to the registered projector
docs_builder/browser_config.py and docs-viewer-config-controller.js Project and normalize sub-scope manifest/by-ID locations Add the access-projected customisation descriptor
docs-subscope-report.js Owns manifest membership, title/group filtering, list/detail navigation, exact refresh, and one contribution object Keep membership/navigation/title search; remove group knowledge; accept composed contributions
docs-subscope-report-filter.js Applies title-prefix and group predicates together Retain the default title predicate; move group predicate to analysis_tags
docs-viewer-management-subscope-contribution.js Bundles New, row state, selection, Prepare Package, Delete, and lifecycle publication for every sub-scope Become the named default Manage contribution; compose optional custom modules after it
docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js Special-cases canonical docs_subscope and constructs the one Manage contribution Resolve descriptor through the Manage registry and compose it without scope/sub-scope ID conditions
report loaders and report registry Both public and Manage load canonical docs_subscope; only Manage supplies management code Preserve one canonical loader; temporary candidate remains local-only
docs-viewer-action-definitions.js Resolves generic action IDs to document-ID, selection, or scope targets Retain generic ID/selection policy; the report contract adds and validates the exact collection envelope
management capability controller/service Publishes service, scope, lifecycle, and package availability Pass resolved availability to action composition; modules do not infer it from manifests

This trace is a current implementation map, not the target module structure. The target ownership below is authoritative for SSR-1.1 and SSR-1.2.

Target owner Responsibility
docs-viewer/services/docs_subscope_report_customisations.py Strict config object, identity registry, settings validation, access declarations, and manifest projector dispatch
docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/sub_scope.py Default public/Manage rows and safe merge of the selected projector result
site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-report.js Final canonical engine, default title filter/sort/projection, exact navigation, and contribution positions
site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-customisation-registry.js Static public-only identity-to-factory registry; contains no Manage imports
docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-customisation-registry.js Static Manage identity-to-factory registry and default-plus-custom composition
docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-default-contribution.js Default Manage row state, sorting, actions, selection, and lifecycle publication
docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-analysis-tags.js Analysis/Tags group filter and row presentation only
docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js Resolve the configured descriptor for the mounted exact collection and supply host capabilities/handlers

The existing unsuffixed Manage contribution is superseded at cutover rather than retained as a second path. Temporary candidate files and dispatch are named separately and removed in SSR-1.2.

Builder Projection Contract

The default builder always creates the public {doc_id, title} row and the standard Manage row. last_updated is always present in a Manage row as a string; an absent source value projects as "" and sorts after dated rows.

One selected customisation projector may add data only inside the customisation namespace. It receives the normalized settings and ordered source documents separately for public and Manage access. It cannot remove, rename, reorder, or overwrite docs membership or a default row field. Unknown document IDs, non-object output, or a namespace collision fail the build.

The Analysis/Tags Manage shape becomes:

{
  "customisation": {
    "id": "analysis_tags",
    "data": {"groups": ["subject", "domain", "form", "theme"]}
  },
  "docs": [
    {
      "doc_id": "d-*",
      "title": "Title",
      "ui_status": "",
      "viewable": true,
      "last_updated": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS",
      "customisation": {"group": "subject"}
    }
  ]
}

Rows without a group omit the row customisation object. Analysis/Tags has no public projector, so its public manifest contains neither root nor row customisation data. The manifest ID must equal the resolved browser descriptor ID before a browser module receives the data.

Browser Contribution Contract

The engine resolves at most one collection customisation, but the resolved module may compose reusable helpers. In Manage, a composer always applies the default contribution first and the optional collection contribution second. Each owner receives its own detached host; content is attached only when populated. A custom module cannot replace or clear a default host.

Version 1 freezes these positions and payloads:

Position Payload and rule
Row access, exact collection, immutable normalized document, and detached leading, titlePrefix, and trailing hosts; may return accessibleLabels
Filter access, exact collection, immutable customisation data, and a filter descriptor with stable id, initialValue, render({host, value, setValue}), and pure matches({document, value})
List toolbar access, exact collection, current visible sorted documents, detached host, {mode, setMode} sort controller, action registrar, and exact refresh callbacks
Selection exact collection, current visible sorted documents, immutable {active, eligibleDocIds, checkedDocIds} snapshot, detached selection-action host, and action registrar
Detail toolbar access, exact collection, manifest document, validated by-ID target, detached host, action registrar, and exact refresh callbacks
Lifecycle mount, refresh, projection, selection, state, and unmount events carrying exact collection identity and the event-specific fields below

The default title predicate and all active custom predicates are applied before the selected sort. The engine owns the complete manifest records, filter state, sorting, and projection. A custom filter changes its own value only through setValue; it cannot mutate records or selection. Selection consumes the current visible sorted projection, while checked IDs remain stable across filter and sort changes.

Lifecycle event fields are:

  • mount: access, collection, and root;
  • refresh: complete normalized documents, customisation data, and reason;
  • projection: visible sorted documents, active sort, immutable filter values, and reason;
  • selection: the immutable selection snapshot and reason;
  • state: state, reason, nullable validated target, refreshDocument(target), and refreshCollection(collection); and
  • unmount: reason.

Callback or predicate failure is contained as a report error. The composer cleans up all mounted owners and does not rerun the report without the selected customisation.

Version 1 provides row adornment/metadata hosts rather than an arbitrary table schema. If Projects later proves that true additional columns are required, the generic contribution contract can add a versioned column position without putting Projects fields or conditions into the default engine.

Action, Target, And Refresh Contract

Every default or custom action is registered in code with id, placement, targetKind, capability, emptyState, handler, and refreshEffect. Configuration and manifests cannot register actions.

The report target kinds are deliberately more specific than the current generic action resolver:

  • collection: exactly {scope, sub_scope};
  • selection: exactly {scope, sub_scope, doc_ids}, where IDs are the explicitly checked collection members; and
  • validated-detail: exactly {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} after membership and by-ID payload identity agree.

The report may use the generic action definitions to resolve an action ID and selection policy, then must wrap the result in the mounted collection and validate the exact keys. It never falls back to the parent scope, active index document, report host, URL text, or an unchecked row.

Default action Placement Target Empty state Availability owner Refresh effect
New List toolbar collection Enabled when creation is available Manage host's exact-collection create handler Rebuild, refresh complete manifest, verify one created target, open it
Prepare Package Selection menu selection Disabled with no checked IDs Document-package capability and handler None
Delete Detail toolbar validated-detail Not rendered outside validated detail Delete workflow capability check Commit exact deletion, reconcile membership, return to list
Copy Link Detail toolbar validated-detail Not rendered outside validated detail Browser clipboard support None

Custom actions use the same target kinds and refresh effects. A missing capability produces only the action's declared omitted or disabled state; it does not prevent the default report or unrelated contributions from mounting. Import remains app-level and receives exact lifecycle targets rather than a registered report action.

Toolbar Ownership

The default Manage contribution owns New, sorting, status/viewability row presentation, selection, Prepare Package, validated-detail Delete and Copy Link, plus collection publication for app-level Import.

An optional customisation owns only its additional controls and presentation. It may reuse common helpers, but those helpers do not activate themselves based on manifest shape or a known collection ID.

The single app-level Import action remains outside the report toolbar. A mounted report may publish its exact collection and refresh callbacks through the standard lifecycle seam; it does not create another Import button.

Analysis/Tags Retrofit

Analysis/Tags becomes one registered customisation of the default report.

The default provides the complete baseline defined above. The Analysis/Tags module adds only its configured group field, group order, and group filter. The builder-side customisation projects group into the Manage manifest; the browser-side customisation renders and applies the group controls. The public manifest remains {doc_id, title} and therefore has no group filter.

Manage title Tags and public title Concepts remain resolved collection configuration, not a new report type. No analysis, tags, concept, or known group value belongs in the default engine or customisation dispatcher.

The refactor removes superseded direct wiring after parity is proven. It does not retain a hidden legacy Tags route alongside the registered module.

Lifecycle Integration

The New sub-scope lifecycle creates a collection with no customisation identity. It also creates one associated parent report host and valid empty public-safe and Manage projections, then refreshes configuration and parent discovery before navigating to the exact returned host.

The association between lifecycle-created collection and host is explicit and stable. Later deletion previews and applies against that exact association; it must not infer the host from title, filename, active document, or URL text.

Post-commit refresh or navigation failure returns the committed identities and retries follow-through only. It never creates another collection or host.

Projects Decision Boundary

The dotlineform/projects collection first receives the default through the normal lifecycle. Its real documents and management workflow are then reviewed before any Projects module is designed.

Possible differences—metadata, grouping, status, sorting, filters, or actions—are evidence prompts, not assumed requirements. The decision may be that the default is sufficient. If customisation is justified, Projects uses the same config identity, registry, contribution positions, exact targets, and public/Manage boundary as Analysis/Tags.

Decisions Owned By Delivery

SSR-1.0 freezes:

  • the exact sub-scope config field and registry shape;
  • the paired builder/browser registration contract for a customisation;
  • contribution placement and lifecycle payloads; and
  • the final module ownership and filenames after current-code inspection.

The default surface, standard Manage row including last_updated, initial title order, recency toggle, Copy Link semantics, and Analysis/Tags group-only customisation are part of that contract. SSR-1.1 implements it through the isolated candidate; SSR-1.2 moves Analysis/Tags and cuts over only after parity.

The second delivery freezes the lifecycle association and failure shape. The third decides only the Projects-specific needs that can be justified from the working default.

The feature parent owns delivery order and status.
